title: Durable dispatch obligation: a root lane that ends a turn holding an executable next action is automatically re-woken when its blocker clears, or carries an explicit blocker and release condition visible in host state
outcome: Durable dispatch obligation: a root lane that ends a turn holding an executable next action is automatically re-woken when its blocker clears, or carries an explicit blocker and release condition visible in host state
acceptance: When a root lane ends a turn, its retained next action is recorded durably as either (a) runnable now, which the host re-wakes automatically within a bounded time, or (b) blocked, with a named blocker and a machine-checkable release condition (for example: a named test run has ended; a full gate's currentStage is past rust/scale; a named mailbox reply has arrived). Tests cover both, and a lane with neither is flagged as a dispatch defect.

When a recorded release condition becomes true, the host wakes the lane with its retained next action within a bounded time, without a coordinator message, and the wake survives a host restart (tests at each persistence cut).

The lane's dispatch state (next action, blocker, release condition, since-when) is visible in host state or the UI and in a status query, so an idle lane never needs a status query to reveal it (test).

Shared-slot release conditions (the warm, cold and gate slots under the build-cap policy) are expressible, so a lane queued for a build slot is woken in queue order when the slot frees, rather than by a coordinator's manual GO.
